q: ____ deals with the quantities in chemical reactions taking place in solutions such as to prepare solutions of desirable concentrations, to carry out chemical reactions using correct amount of solutions, and to predict the amount produced in solutions.
e: Solution stoichiometry deals with the quantities in chemical reactions taking place in solutions such as to prepare solutions of desirable concentrations, to carry out chemical reactions using correct amount of solutions, and to predict the amount produced in solutions. Stoichiometry is the quantitative bookkeeping of how much of each substance takes part in a reaction.

q: To measure volume, chemists use ____ ($dm^3$) or litre (L) as the standard unit.
e: To measure volume, chemists use cubic decimetre (dm^3) or litre (L) as the standard unit. The SI base unit of length is the metre, symbol m. One litre is the same volume as one cubic decimetre, which is also 1000 mL or 1000 cm3.

q: ____ of a solution is the quantity in moles of solute dissolved in one cubic decimetre ($1 \text{ dm}^3$) of solution.
e: Molarity (M) of a solution is the quantity in moles of solute dissolved in one cubic decimetre (1 dm^3) of solution. The SI base unit of length is the metre, symbol m. Molarity is moles of solute per cubic decimetre of solution. One litre is the same volume as one cubic decimetre, which is also 1000 mL or 1000 cm3.

q: A ____ of a compound is a solution which contains one mole of the compound in one cubic decimetre ($1 \text{ dm}^3$) of the solution.
e: A molar solution of a compound is a solution which contains one mole of the compound in one cubic decimetre (1 dm^3) of the solution. One mole is the amount that holds as many particles as 12 g of carbon-12, which is 6.02 x 10^23 particles. The SI base unit of length is the metre, symbol m. One litre is the same volume as one cubic decimetre, which is also 1000 mL or 1000 cm3.

q: ____ is the procedure for preparing a less concentrated solution from a more concentrated one.

q: The formula for dilution is ____.

q: In volumetric analysis, the term ____ is used for the procedure in which a solution of a standard reagent (reactant) is added to a specific volume of a solution of unknown molarity.
e: In volumetric analysis, the term titration is used for the procedure in which a solution of a standard reagent (reactant) is added to a specific volume of a solution of unknown molarity. Titration adds a standard solution of known concentration until the reaction with an unknown is complete. Molarity is moles of solute per cubic decimetre of solution.

q: The reagent of exactly known concentration that is used in a titration is called a ____.
e: The reagent of exactly known concentration that is used in a titration is called a standard solution. Titration adds a standard solution of known concentration until the reaction with an unknown is complete.

q: A ____ is a highly pure and stable compound, used to establish the concentration of the standard solution.
e: A primary standard is a highly pure and stable compound, used to establish the concentration of the standard solution. Stable compound, used to establish the concentration of the standard solution.

q: The common types of titrations are: ____ (neutralisation titration), precipitation titration, oxidation-reduction titration (redox titration) and complexometric titration.
e: The common types of titrations are: acid-base titration (neutralisation titration), precipitation titration, oxidation-reduction titration (redox titration) and complexometric titration. Titration adds a standard solution of known concentration until the reaction with an unknown is complete. Redox is electron transfer: oxidation is loss of electrons and reduction is gain of electrons. Precipitation titration forms a solid, alongside acid-base, redox and complexometric titrations.
